title: Late Breaking Results: LLM-assisted Automated Incremental Proof Generation for Hardware Verification
problem: Hardware verification requires extensive manual effort in defining module invariants and integration properties. Proof generation for incrementally composed designs lacks automation, limiting scalability.
motivation: Automating hardware verification can reduce manual effort and improve verification efficiency and correctness of complex designs.
method: The system uses an LLM to break a hardware design into basic building blocks and prove each correct incrementally. For each block, the LLM writes invariants (rules about what must always be true, like 'this adder won't overflow') and verifies them using Z3 (an automated theorem prover). As blocks combine, the LLM also verifies that boundaries between them connect correctly. The system was tested on arithmetic circuits including Ripple Carry Adders and Dadda Tree Multipliers.
key_novelty: LLMs automate proof generation for hardware verification for the first time by working incrementally—each module gets correctness rules written by the LLM and verified by Z3, a logic verification tool.
contributions: LLM-assisted methodology for incremental proof generation in hardware verification
Automated invariant definition and formal verification using LLMs and Z3
Integration property formulation at module interfaces
Case studies demonstrating improved efficiency on arithmetic circuits
